tei:titleStmt.tei:title: שִׁיר לְצִיּוֹן
Shir l'Tsiyōn — a hymn celebrating the reïfication of the Balfour Declaration at the culmination of the San Remo conference on 11 May 1920 by Rabbi Jacob Gerstein

tei:div.tei:head: Shir l'Tsiyōn — a hymn celebrating the reïfication of the Balfour Declaration at the culmination of the San Remo conference on 11 May 1920 by Rabbi Jacob Gerstein

tei:lg.tei:l: In 1920, the 11th of May,
We were told: “Go!”
Marching through all the streets,
Sorrow turned to joy,
Oy! we have already suffered enough tsures,
Little Yisroel, carry your banner of Ẓíōn,
Your exile has already reached its limit,
You have regained your country,
Enough mockery and shame already,
Ẓíōn calls her children home,
Everyone sees already, even a blind man,
That Erets Yisroel is already for the Yidden,
Of many kinds of trouble he has already had enough.
Yid-ele, Yid-ele!......
Take already your fidd-le,
Play already your song-ele,
in the Beit ha-Miqdosh — the shir!
And also pray to God for me,
That I may rejoice in sympathy with you.
We have, after all, the same father.
Once we sheltered ourselves beneath one shadow,
You are indeed my blood and flesh,
It’s true that we cast you into the water and fire,
But now we shall help you,
From your Holy Land you shall drink your wine.
Yisroel, Yisroel! arise now from your sleep,
Go, offer sacrifices — a sheep and an ox,
We will always be good to you all,
For we know your worth and your virtue.
Even in all the bad times,
You never wished to barter away your faith,
Even when you were tormented and hunted,
You spoke the very same words:
Shema’ Yisroel, Hashem Eloheinu, Hashem Eḥad,
Hear, Yid-ele — God, our God, is One,
He does everything, not anyone else,
By His command He breaks the bones of the enemies of Yisroel.
Now for you, Yid-ele, there is a great joy,
You are already taking leave of your long exile,
For 2,000 years you wandered around the whole world,
Whether in great heat or in great cold,
And you always cried out: “Next year in Jerusalem!”
But now from Heaven salvation has already come.

tei:note.tei:p: The proposed treaty crafted at the San Remo conference in April 1920 was presented to Ottoman Empire officials in Paris on 11 May 1920.

Likely, a reference to the legendary shir ḥadash — the new song said to be sung in the future (per Rashi on Psalms 96:1), i.e., in the era of the Moshiaḥ. Alternately, a non-specific reference to any of the contextually relevant psalms beginning with שיר, e.g. Psalms 126.
Acknowledging that as a Jew living outside the Land of Israel, his joy is secondary.
The eponymous Yisrael, the patriarch Yaaqov (Jacob). Cf. Genesis 32:29.

Possibly a reference to religious objections to political Zionism in the land of Israel for varied reasons among both orthodox and heterodox Jews in the Diaspora at the time, including in the United States. For “water” and “fire,” compare the confessional prayer Unetaneh Toqef, “מִי בַמַּֽיִם וּמִי בָאֵשׁ” (“who [will die] by water, who [will die] by fire”), the purpose of the Days of Judgement and Atonement being to collectively atone for the transgressions of the community to avoid decrees of earthly suffering at the hands of others (other nations, etc.).
As the last words uttered before expiring, per Jewish tradition.
Numbers 24:8. Also, following the metaphor of bones as elements of support, find Berakhot 32a.2 and Berakhot 4b.21-22 where raising up Israel follows from bringing about their enemies downfall.
